evidence.curator_note: RE-ENCODED 2026-07-28. Through-space H rearrangement onto the ionized amine nitrogen N(9): the odd electron on that site pairs with one electron of the C(5)-H bond to form the new heteroatom-H bond, and the second C-H electron is left on C(5) as the new radical terminus. ARC COUNT: the book draws 2 single-barbed fishhooks on this branch - one from the '+.' on the heteroatom arcing toward the forming heteroatom...H region (= move <1>), one from the central C-H bond curling up to the same point (= move <2>) - and the third hook (move <3>, the other C-H electron onto C(5)) is an IMPLICIT homolysis hook required for electron balance, not drawn on the page. CORRECTION vs the previous version, which was judged unfaithful: it encoded only ONE move, a heavy-atom net electron relocation (9 -> 5) that transcribed NEITHER drawn arc, and justified the collapse by asserting that 'the migrating hydrogen cannot carry an atom map because RDKit folds a mapped explicit [H:n] into the heavy atom's implicit valence'. That justification is FALSE as stated: it holds for a bare [H:n], but the corpus's standard workaround is the ISOTOPE-TAGGED [1H:n], which RDKit keeps as a real mapped atom - it is used in 80 of the records, and IMS8-EQ8.19 encodes this very reaction type with the full three-hook flow via [1H:8]. The migrating hydrogen is therefore now carried explicitly as [1H:10] and the complete balanced three-move flow is encoded, matching IMS8-EQ8.19. Protium-1 is ordinary hydrogen, so no mass is altered. ms_context: p202 prints NO ionization conditions for Eq 8.88; ionization_method 'EI' / electron_energy_ev 70.0 are the book's STANDING convention applied as a chapter default, NOT data read off this page (disclosed here, as sibling IMS8-EQ8.89 does).

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.88 (its Chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14), so no equation-indexed MOD rule exists for this scheme. The un-indexed GENERIC rule hTransition_saturated_1 (src/data_generation/rules/IMS_bookCover.py, name 'H transition receptor site saturated §Y6', DFS '[H]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[_A+.]6 >> [C.]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[_A+]6[H]1') describes exactly this step, with the element wildcard _A instantiated as nitrogen: the ionized saturated receptor takes the hydrogen from the carbon four bonds away (six-membered TS), leaving a carbon radical and an even-electron ammonium -- the same bond changes (C-H broken, N-H formed, no heavy-atom bond order changed, radical relocated from N to C) as the dashed arcs drawn here. VERIFIED rather than asserted (convention E): the term-mode rule was applied to this record's instantiated precursor inside the project container (mod.DG one-step apply, LabelType.Term/Specialisation) and returns 'C(CC[CH.]CCC[NH3+])O', i.e. HO-(CH2)3-CH(.)-(CH2)3-NH3+ -- exactly the product species encoded here (2 derivations, one per hydrogen of the central CH2). Cross-linked as computationally supported, with the caveat that the rule is generic and carries no equation id, so it is not a book-authored 8.88 rule. Note also what the rule does NOT capture: because _A is a bare element wildcard, hTransition_saturated_1 fires at whichever heteroatom happens to be ionized and encodes no proton-affinity ordering, so it cannot express the competition between the two receptor sites that Equation 8.88 exists to illustrate, nor the product-to-product interconversion the book draws with the vertical arrows. hTransition_unsaturated was checked and does NOT apply (it requires a double bond between receptor and neighbour).
